clue.text: Synthetic cream's over the side

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters of the two words before it are tumbled into a fresh order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter; it stands for 'is' joining the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: Artificial cream has spilled over the edge of the bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Synthetic' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: all fourteen letters of SYNTHETIC CREAM are rearranged, with 'over' as the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester City is a football club, and a team in sport is called a side.

clue.text: Elementary particle on tuner replaced

indicators.note: replaced here means put back in a different arrangement, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: A physicist's tiny particle sits on a radio tuner that has been swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the subatomic building blocks of the atom, an uncharged particle found in the nucleus.

clue.text: Backward animal

explanation.surface: A creature that is slow on the uptake.
explanation.definitionFit: Hind means rear, at the back, as in hind legs; a hind is also a female deer.

clue.text: Individual entering theatre during early period

indicators.note: one word going into another means it sits inside the other's letters

parts.note: the stage is the acting profession, the theatre in general
an individual is a single one

explanation.surface: A lone actor walks into a playhouse in some bygone era.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric era when tools were made of flint is an early period of human history.

clue.text: Lure medical specialist onto rink

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital speciality and its doctor
a rink is a sheet of ice for skating

explanation.surface: Tempting a doctor out on to the skating rink.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt or coax someone into doing something; a lure is a temptation.

clue.text: But this store does not have a monopoly

definitions.text: But this store does not have a monopoly

parts.words: But this store does not have a monopoly
parts.note: to corner a market is to monopolise it, yet the small local grocer named after a street angle has no such power

explanation.surface: A remark that a small shop is no monopolist.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke rests on 'corner the market', meaning to gain a monopoly; a British corner shop is a small local grocery on a street corner.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small neighbourhood shop selling everyday groceries, typically sited where two streets meet.

clue.text: Finished with a boring activity?

explanation.surface: Done with something tedious at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like 'dull' but means drilling: a drill goes right through the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Through means done, as in 'I'm through'; a drill that bores penetrates from one side to the other.

clue.text: One in Caen asking for it to be easy

parts.note: Caen is a French city, and the French for one is un
demanding something is asking for it insistently

explanation.surface: A French speaker requests that the task be made simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easy makes few calls on one's effort or skill, a relaxed and simple task.

clue.text: Traitor to go round with Tom catching ball

parts.note: to turn is to go round, rotate

indicators.note: one piece holding another means the other goes inside it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
the letter O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A turncoat cat circles about, pouncing on a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deserts their side or party for the opposition, a defector.

clue.text: Engineers rush to repeat showing

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
to rush is to run

explanation.surface: Army engineers hurry along to see a programme again.
explanation.definitionFit: A second broadcast of a programme already aired is a repeat on television.

clue.text: Stay with the French footballer or swimmer

parts.note: to stay put is to stick
le is French for 'the'
a back is a defending player in football

explanation.surface: Stay with the French side as a player or a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spiny fish found in rivers and ponds, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Army and navy pool

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The army and navy share a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain lake, a pool of still water in the hills of northern England.

clue.text: Again plan here 500 clues to be rewritten

indicators.note: to rewrite something is to set it down differently, so these letters go into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A setter resolves to redo five hundred clues here.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a new time for an event is to plan it afresh, often postponing it.

clue.text: Solitary nipper?

parts.note: read as a lonely little child, but a nipper is also a pincered creature, and this one lives alone in a borrowed shell

explanation.surface: A lonely little child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' is British slang for a small child, but here it means something that nips with claws.
explanation.definitionFit: A crustacean that lives inside an empty seashell, naming it after a recluse, and it pinches with its claws.

clue.text: Come together with hundred at roadside

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
on can mean at, as in 'on the spot'
the verge is the grassy strip along the edge of a British road

explanation.surface: People gather in their hundreds by the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or crowds that meet at one point are joining up, meeting from different directions.

clue.text: Mat has aggravated breathing complaint

indicators.note: aggravated means stirred up and disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dusty mat has made someone's breathing trouble worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronic condition where the airways narrow, causing wheezing and shortness of breath.

clue.text: Lady had most of the quartz

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but its final letter

parts.note: cornelian, also spelt carnelian, is a reddish variety of quartz

explanation.surface: A woman owned the greater part of the gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's given name, borne by the Roman matron mother of the Gracchi.

clue.text: Vegetable to stick inside shelter

indicators.note: the second piece is placed within the letters of the first

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
gum is glue, something used to stick

explanation.surface: A vegetable glued to the inside of a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas, beans and lentils are pod-bearing plants used as vegetables.

clue.text: Girl took in article, striped cotton fabric

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
to take in food is to eat it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl took in a piece of striped cloth to be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong striped cotton material once used for sailor suits and children's clothes.

clue.text: Respected our Edward who had not been paid first

indicators.note: this piece is put at the front, ahead of the others

parts.note: Hon. is short for honorary, describing an unpaid post such as an honorary secretary
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Our Edward, an unpaid volunteer, was held in esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hon.' abbreviates honorary, an office held without a salary, which the clue spells out at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone honoured is held in high esteem, regarded with admiration.

clue.text: Automatic singular science?

indicators.note: making the word singular drops the S that looks like a plural ending

parts.note: robotics is the science of building automated machines

explanation.surface: A strange science that seems to run on autopilot.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of the science ends in S, which the clue treats as a plural ending; 'singular' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanical and without thought, like a machine going through its motions.

clue.text: Frost about to go all round peninsula

indicators.note: the outer piece encircles the other, so the frost word sits inside

parts.note: ca. is short for circa, Latin for about
rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: Frost is set to cover the whole of a peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: A large landmass on the Black Sea joined to the mainland by a narrow neck, a peninsula.

clue.text: Propping up pillow in middle of night

parts.note: a bolster is a long pillow

indicators.note: the centre letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Lying awake at night, plumping up a pillow.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting or reinforcing something, as a cushion holds up a sleeper.

clue.text: No boycott for port

parts.note: O, the figure nought, means none at all
a ban is a prohibition, as a boycott is

explanation.surface: A harbour town refuses to join a trade boycott.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a Scottish west coast ferry port, gateway to the Hebrides.

clue.text: It might be written in haste to printers

definitions.text: It might be written in haste to printers

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A hurried note scribbled to the print shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an editor writes this proof mark to tell printers to leave a deleted correction as it was.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'let it stand', a proofreader's mark cancelling an earlier correction.

clue.text: More appealing price reduction made with hesitation

parts.note: a cut is a reduction in price
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A discount offered with some reluctance looks more attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means charming, endearing, so more appealing is the comparative form.

clue.text: Fight for title I am arranging

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters into a different order

explanation.surface: A boxer campaigns for a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To militate is to work or campaign forcefully, struggling against or for something.

clue.text: Greek character has piece that is the lightest of the hyperons

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet
a particle is a tiny piece of something

explanation.surface: A Greek letter has a fragment that is the smallest of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperons are heavy subatomic baryons, and the neutral one named after a Greek letter has the least mass of them.
